cues.zh: 每次演讲开头都感谢大家，我都觉得自己像在反复播放同一张唱片。
cues.en: I feel like a broken record every time I start these talks by thanking everybody.

cues.zh: 所以这次我想换个方式开场：我儿子今天要结婚了。
cues.en: So I want to start this talk in a different way by saying, my son is getting married today.

cues.zh: 在
cues.en: in

cues.zh: 另一个
cues.en: another

cues.zh: 州。
cues.en: state.

cues.zh: 所以这场演讲一结束，我就要赶飞机。
cues.en: So right after I give this talk, I'm going to hop on a plane.

cues.zh: 去参加婚礼，明天早上回来。
cues.en: Go do that, and I'll be back tomorrow morning.

cues.zh: 所以我并没有消失。
cues.en: So I haven't disappeared.

cues.zh: 我很期待后续的演讲和其他环节，不过我会短暂缺席一下。
cues.en: I am looking forward to the follow-up talks and everything else, but I will be missing in action briefly.

cues.zh: 呃，所以现在再重复一下。
cues.en: Uh, so now to be redundant.

cues.zh: 谢谢大家来参加。
cues.en: Thanks everybody for coming.

cues.zh: 10 年前 Clojure 发布时，我完全无法想象
cues.en: 10 years ago closure was released, and there's no possible way.

cues.zh: 会发展到今天这样。
cues.en: I could have imagined this.

cues.zh: 呃，你知道，我跟妻子 Steph 说，如果有 100 个人用它，那就离谱得不可思议了。
cues.en: Uh, you know, I told my wife, Steph, I said, if 100 people use this, that would be ridiculously outrageous.

cues.zh: 嗯，呃，但事情并不是那样。
cues.en: Um, and uh that's not what happened.

cues.zh: 实际发生的事，嗯，挺有意思的。
cues.en: And what did happen is, happened is uh, is interesting.

cues.zh: 我不认为大家完全理解它。
cues.en: I don't think it's fully understood.

cues.zh: 嗯，但今天我想聊聊，稍微回顾一下 Clojure 背后的动机。
cues.en: Uh, but I wanted today to talk about um, a look back a little bit about the motivations behind closure.

cues.zh: 嗯，这不像你推出一种编程语言时，就能把整个故事讲清楚。
cues.en: Uh, it's not like when you come out with a programming language, you can you can tell that whole story.

cues.zh: 我想，一是因为这不适合做营销。
cues.en: I think one because it's not good marketing.

cues.zh: 二是因为，如果你真说实话，你大概自己也不知道。
cues.en: And two, because if you really want to be honest, you probably don't know.

cues.zh: 嗯，要理解发生了什么、为什么会这样，以及你当时真正在想什么，是需要时间的。
cues.en: Uh, it takes time to understand what happened and why, and what you really were thinking.

cues.zh: 我不会假装自己有个宏大计划，把所有最终成为 Clojure 的东西都纳入其中。
cues.en: And I won't pretend that I had a grand plan that incorporated everything that ended up becoming closure.

cues.zh: 它肯定涉及与社区里很多人的互动。
cues.en: It certainly involved a lot of interaction with people in the community.

cues.zh: 嗯，但确实有这么一点。
cues.en: Um, but there is this.

cues.zh: Clojure 是很有主见的。
cues.en: Closure is opinionated.

cues.zh: 这个，我们常听到。
cues.en: This, we hear this.

cues.zh: 呃，我觉得从两个方面来想很有意思。
cues.en: Uh, and I think it's interesting to think about two aspects of that.

cues.zh: 嗯，一个是它在哪些方面如此，以及一门语言“有主见”意味着什么。
cues.en: Um, one is in which ways is it, and what does it mean for a language to be opinionated.

cues.zh: 呃，我觉得在 Clojure 的情况下，人们接触它时会说，哇，你知道吗，我每转一个弯它都在逼我按某种方式做事。
cues.en: Uh, I think in closure's case, uh, people come to it and they're like, wow, you know, this is forcing me everywhere I turn to do something a certain way.

cues.zh: 呃，所以我觉得好一点的说法是：它只强力支持少数几种惯用法，并为它们提供大量支持。
cues.en: Uh, so and I think that the nice way to say that is there's only a few strongly supported idioms and a lot of support for them.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你用它自带的东西，就有一整套配套方案支持你的做法。
cues.en: So, you know, if you use the stuff that comes with it, there's a whole story that supports your efforts.

cues.zh: 如果你想跟它对着干，呃，我们也不会做太多。
cues.en: And if you want to fight against that, uh, we don't do too much.

cues.zh: Alex 问我哪副眼镜才是对的，呃，答案是都不对。
cues.en: Alex was asking me which glasses are the right ones and uh, neither is the answer.

cues.zh: 呃，但设计就是做取舍，而 Clojure 里有很多取舍。
cues.en: Uh, but but design is about making choices and, you know, there's a bunch of choices in closure.

cues.zh: 尤其是，有一个很大的取舍：要舍弃什么。
cues.en: In particular, there's a big choice about what to leave out.

cues.zh: 这次演讲的一部分，就会讲哪些东西被舍弃了。
cues.en: And part of this talk will be talking about what was left out.

cues.zh: 呃，有主见的另一面是，你知道，你怎么变得有主见？
cues.en: Uh, the other side of being opinionated is, you know, how do you get opinionated?

cues.zh: 我是说，又不是说我有主见。
cues.en: I mean, it's not like I'm opinionated.

cues.zh: 当然，我就是有主见。
cues.en: Of course, I'm opinionated.

cues.zh: 呃，这来自经验。
cues.en: Uh, and that comes from experience.

cues.zh: 呃，2005 年我开始做 Clojure 的时候。
cues.en: Uh, when I started uh, doing closure, uh, in 2005.

cues.zh: 我已经写了 18 年代码，所以我受够了。
cues.en: I had already been programming for 18 years, so I had had it.

cues.zh: 我不想再干了。
cues.en: I was done.

cues.zh: 我厌倦了。
cues.en: I was tired of it.

cues.zh: 呃，但我用当时专业程序员使用的语言，做过一些非常有意思的事。
cues.en: Uh, but I had done some really interesting things uh, with the with, you know, the languages that professional programmers used at the time.

cues.zh: 呃，主要是在用 C++ 做调度系统。
cues.en: Uh, so primarily I was working on scheduling systems in C++.

cues.zh: 这些是给广播机构用的排期系统，所以电台会用排期系统来决定播放哪些音乐。
cues.en: These are scheduling systems for broadcasters, so radio stations use scheduling systems to determine what music they play.

cues.zh: 它的运作方式相当精巧。
cues.en: And it's quite sophisticated, the way that works.

cues.zh: 你想啊，在一天当中，你不想重复播放同一首歌。
cues.en: You know, you think about, well, over the course of the day, you don't want to repeat the same song.

cues.zh: 你还得考虑那些人：他们早上听一小时广播，下午另一个小时也听。
cues.en: You actually have to think about the people who, you know, listen to the radio for one hour in the morning and this other hour in the afternoon.

cues.zh: 而且你要为每个通勤时段创建一种平行时间维度。
cues.en: And you create sort of an alternate time dimension for every drive time hour.

cues.zh: 呃，诸如此类。
cues.en: Uh, and things like that.

cues.zh: 所以就有了多维排期，我们用进化程序优化，呃，来做排期优化。
cues.en: So there's multi-dimensional scheduling and we used evolutionary program, uh, optimization to do uh, schedule optimization.

cues.zh: 呃，广播自动化就是播放音频，当时我们就在做这个。
cues.en: Uh, broadcast automation is about playing audio, and at the time, we were doing this.

cues.zh: 呃，在电脑上播放音频曾经很难。
cues.en: Uh, playing audio on computers was a hard thing.

cues.zh: 它需要专用的呃，声卡来做呃，做 DSP 处理。
cues.en: It required dedicated uh, cards to do uh, to do the DSP work.

cues.zh: 呃，我做过音频指纹，所以我们做的系统放在壁橱里监听广播。
cues.en: Uh, I did work on audio fingerprinting, so we made systems that sat in closets and listened to the radio.

cues.zh: 然后记下它们听到的内容。
cues.en: And and wrote down what they heard.

cues.zh: 呃，这既用来跟踪电台歌单，最终也用来跟踪广告，而广告才是赚钱的地方。
cues.en: Uh, and this was both used to track station playlists, and then eventually to track the advertising, which is where the money was for that.

cues.zh: 呃，这涉及嗯，想办法高效地提取音频指纹、清洗音频，把新内容与过去做比较。
cues.en: Uh, which involved um, figuring out how to effectively fingerprint audio and scrub audio, sort of compare novelty to the past.

cues.zh: 嗯，我做过收益管理系统。
cues.en: Um, I worked on yield management systems.

cues.zh: 呃，大家都知道收益管理是什么吗？
cues.en: Uh, does everybody know what yield management is?

cues.zh: 大概不知道。
cues.en: Probably not.

cues.zh: 那呃，酒店、航空公司和电台有什么共同点？
cues.en: So what do uh, hotels, airlines, and radio stations have in common?

cues.zh: 它们的库存会随着时间消失。
cues.en: Their inventory disappears as time passes.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 你有，哦，我有一间空房，你知道，我日程里有个空档，这架飞机上有个座位。
cues.en: You have, oh, I have a free room, you know, I've got a slot in my schedule, I've got a seat on this airplane.

cues.zh: 然后时间流逝，没人买它，现在你就没有了。
cues.en: And then time passes and nobody bought it, and now you don't.

cues.zh: 呃，所以收益管理是一门实践科学，试图弄清楚如何在库存从你眼皮底下消失时优化它的价值。
cues.en: Uh, so yield management is the science in in practice of uh, trying to figure out how to optimize the value of your inventory as it disappears after from under you.

cues.zh: 呃，这关乎回顾过去和过往销售，而且并不简单。
cues.en: And that's about uh, looking at the past and past sales, and it's not simplistic.

cues.zh: 所以，比如，目标并不是卖掉所有库存。
cues.en: So for instance, it's not an objective to sell all of your inventory.

cues.zh: 目标是最大化你从中获得的收入，这意味着大多数情况下不能全部卖掉。
cues.en: The objective is to maximize the amount of revenue you get you get from it, which means not selling all of it in most cases.

cues.zh: 嗯，那不是用 C++ 写的，那大概是在我发现 Common Lisp 的时候，也就是那 15 年里的第 8 年左右。
cues.en: Um, that was not written in uh, C++, that was around the time I discovered common Lisp, which was about eight years into that 15 years.

cues.zh: 而且呃，这个的使用方根本不可能去用 Common Lisp。
cues.en: And uh, there was no way the consumer of this would use common Lisp.

cues.zh: 于是我写了一个 Common Lisp 程序，把所有收益管理算法重新生成成 SQL 存储过程，再把这个数据库交给他们——而这个数据库本身就是一个程序。
cues.en: So I wrote a common Lisp program that wrote all the yield management algorithms again out as a SQL store procedures and gave them this database, which was a program.

cues.zh: 呃，最终我又回到调度问题，用 Common Lisp 写了一种新的调度系统，而他们又一次不想把它跑在生产环境里。
cues.en: Uh, eventually I got back to scheduling and again wrote a new kind of scheduling uh, system in common Lisp, which again they did not want to run in production.

cues.zh: 嗯，然后我用 C++ 重写了它。
cues.en: Um, and then I rewrote it in C++.

cues.zh: 到这时，我已经是 C++ 专家级用户，而且——按某种“爱”的定义——真的很爱 C++。
cues.en: Now at this point, I was an expert C++ user and really loved C++ for some value of love.

cues.zh: 那种爱完全不包含任何满足感。
cues.en: That involves no satisfaction at all.

cues.zh: 呃，但后面我们会看到，我喜欢 C++ 带来的解谜乐趣。
cues.en: Uh, but as we'll see later, I love the puzzle of C++.

cues.zh: 呃，所以我不得不用 C++ 重写它，结果重写花的时间是当初写它的四倍，代码量是五倍，而且一点也没变快。
cues.en: Uh, so I had to rewrite it in C++, and it took, you know, four times as long to rewrite it as it took to write it in the first place, it yielded five times as much code and it was no faster.

cues.zh: 那时我才意识到自己做错了。
cues.en: And that's when I knew I was doing it wrong.

cues.zh: 后来我帮朋友 Eric 编写了美国全国出口民调系统的新版本，其中还涉及选举预测系统。
cues.en: Uh, went on to help uh, my friend Eric write the new version of the national exit poll system for the US, which also involves an election projection system.

cues.zh: 我们用的是，你知道，一种自定的函数式 C# 风格。
cues.en: We did that in, you know, a sort of self-imposed functional uh, style of C Sharp.

cues.zh: 然后，你知道，大概 2005 年，我开始做 Clojure，同时还在做一个机器听觉项目。
cues.en: Um, and then, you know, around 2005, I started doing closure, and this machine listening project at the same time.

cues.zh: 我给自己放了两年假，专门做这些事。
cues.en: And I had given myself a two year sabbatical to work on these things.

cues.zh: 当时不知道它们会各自走向何方，也让自己自由地做我认为对的事。
cues.en: Uh, not knowing which one uh, would go where and leaving myself free to do whatever I thought was right.

cues.zh: 所以我没有商业目标，也没有验收指标。
cues.en: So I had zero commercial objectives, zero acceptance metrics.

cues.zh: 那两年我只想让自己满意，算是给自己放了个假。
cues.en: I was trying to please myself for two years, just sort of bought myself a break.

cues.zh: 呃，但在这个过程中，在那段时间里，我意识到自己只来得及完成一个；我知道怎么完成 Clojure，而机器听觉是一个研究课题。
cues.en: Uh, but along the way, during that period of time, you know, I realized I would only have time to finish one, and I knew how to finish closure and that, you know, machine listening is a is a research topic.

cues.zh: 我不知道当时是还差两年，还是还差五年。
cues.en: I don't know if I was two years away or five years away.

cues.zh: 嗯，所以 Clojure 最初是用 Java 写的，后来你知道，库都是用 Clojure 写的。
cues.en: Um, so closure was written in Java and eventually, you know, the libraries are written in closure.

cues.zh: 嗯，机器听觉的工作涉及构建人工耳蜗，我是用 Common Lisp、Mathematica 和 C++ 的组合来做的。
cues.en: Um, and the machine listening work involved building an artificial cochlea, and I did that in a combination of common Lisp and Mathematica, and C++.

cues.zh: 最近几年，我把它重新捡起来时，呃，已经能用 Clojure 来做这件事了，这大概是最让人兴奋的。
cues.en: And in recent years, as I've dusted it off, uh, I've been able to do it in closure, and that's sort of the most exciting thing.

cues.zh: 呃，你知道，以前做这件事我需要这三种语言，而现在我只需要 Clojure 就够了。
cues.en: Uh, you know, I needed these three languages before to do this, and now I only need closure to do it.

cues.zh: 嗯，然后我做了 Atomic，它也是一个闭包。
cues.en: Um, and then I did the Atomic, which was also closure.

cues.zh: 呃，这些项目几乎都涉及数据库。
cues.en: Uh, almost all of these projects involved a database.

cues.zh: 各种各样的数据库，从 IIM 数据库，到大量 SQL，做过很多尝试，但 RDF 的集成并不多。
cues.en: All different kinds of databases, from, you know, IIM databases, a lot of SQL, many attempts, but not many integrations of RDF.

cues.zh: 嗯，数据库是解决这类问题必不可少的一部分。
cues.en: Um, databases are an essential part of solving these kinds of problems.

cues.zh: 而这正是我们做的事。
cues.en: And it's just this is what we do.

cues.zh: 有多少人每天的工作中会用到数据库？
cues.en: How many people use a database in what they do every day?

cues.zh: 有多少人不用？
cues.en: How many people don't?

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 所以最后这个东西并不是数据库的缩写。
cues.en: So this last thing is not an acronym for a database.

cues.zh: 它放在那儿是为了提醒我讲这个轶事。
cues.en: It's there to remind me to tell this anecdote.

cues.zh: 呃，我以前常去轻量级语言研讨会。
cues.en: Uh, so I used to go to the lightweight languages workshop.

cues.zh: 那是在 MIT 举办的一日研讨会，嗯，做小型语言的人——你知道，专有的或者特定领域的，比如 Darp 之类的——会聊聊他们的小语言，以及他们用小语言做些什么。
cues.en: It was a one day workshop held at MIT, um, where people working on small languages, you know, either proprietary or just domain specific, you know, Darp, whatever, would talk about their their little languages and what they were doing with little languages.

cues.zh: 那非常酷，也非常令人兴奋。
cues.en: It was very cool and very exciting.

cues.zh: 把一群编程语言极客聚在同一个房间里。
cues.en: Got a bunch of language geeks in the same room.

cues.zh: 之后还有披萨。
cues.en: And there was pizza afterwards.

cues.zh: 我记得，我要么自己去，要么和朋友一起去；我并不属于那个……做这种事的社群。
cues.en: So I remember, I would just go by myself or with my friend and I'm not I was not part of the community that um, did that.

cues.zh: 他们就这么让我进去了。
cues.en: They just let me in.

cues.zh: 呃，不过后来还有披萨。
cues.en: Uh, but afterwards had pizza.

cues.zh: 于是吃披萨时，我和两个不认识的人坐在一起，到现在也不知道他们叫什么。
cues.en: So I sat down at pizza with two people I didn't know and I still don't know their names.

cues.zh: 他们是计算机语言研究人员。
cues.en: computer language researchers.

cues.zh: 他们也在贬低他们的一位，呃，同行，那人不知怎么跟数据库混到了一起，迷失了正道。
cues.en: and they were talking also disparagingly about their, uh, their associate who'd somehow fallen in with databases and lost the true way.

cues.zh: 幸好我不知道，因为我现在就要贬低他们了。
cues.en: And it's good that I don't, because I'm going to now disparage them.

cues.zh: 呃，他们俩都，呃，
cues.en: Uh, they were both, uh,

cues.zh: 然后，他们中的一个有点嗤笑着对另一个说：
cues.en: And, and one of them sort of sneeringly went to the other and said,

cues.zh: “啊，数据库，你上次用数据库，是什么时候？”
cues.en: "Ah, database, when was the last time you, you used a database?"

cues.zh: 他说：“我不确定自己有没有用过数据库。”
cues.en: He was like, "I don't know that I've ever used a database."

cues.zh: 然后我有点被披萨噎住了
cues.en: And like, I sort of choked on my pizza

cues.zh: 因为按理说，他们是在设计编程语言，可他们编程时从不用数据库。
cues.en: because, theoretically, they're designing programming languages and yet they're programming and they never use databases.

cues.zh: 我不知道这怎么可能。
cues.en: I didn't know how that worked.

cues.zh: 但这某种程度上促成了我去做闭包，因为我的意思是，不做数据库的人也能写编程语言，谁都可以。
cues.en: But it was part of the inspiration to do closure because, I mean, people who don't do databases can write programming languages, anybody can.

cues.zh: 所以，呃，你知道，程序有不同种类；我在幻灯片里想表达的一点，就是我当时在做的那些程序属于哪些种类。
cues.en: So, uh, you know, there are different kinds of programs and one of the things I tried to capture on the slide is to talk about what those kinds of programs were that I was working on.

cues.zh: 我想出的词是“情境化程序”。
cues.en: And the word I came up with were situated programs.

cues.zh: 换句话说，你可以区分出这类程序：它们存在于世界中，并在某种程度上与世界纠缠在一起。
cues.en: In other words, you can distinguish these kinds of programs that sit in the world and are sort of entangled with the world.

cues.zh: 它们有一堆特征。
cues.en: They have a bunch of characteristics.

cues.zh: 一是，呃，它们会长时间运行。不是只算出这个结果然后丢到那边。
cues.en: One is, uh, they execute for an extended period of time. It's not just like calculate this result and spit it over there.

cues.zh: 呃，它不像 AWS 里的 Lambda 函数。
cues.en: Uh, it's not like a Lambda function in AWS.

cues.zh: 这些东西是持续运行的，而且它们，它们算是和外界连在一起的。
cues.en: These things run on an ongoing basis and they're, they're sort of wired up to the world.

cues.zh: 嗯，而且大多数这类系统都是 7×24 小时连续运行。
cues.en: Um, and most of these systems run continuously 24/7.

cues.zh: 让我觉得挺吓人的是，现在这些有 30 年历史的东西，几乎肯定还在某个地方 7×24 小时运行着。
cues.en: It's quite terrifying to me that now these things which are 30 years old, are almost definitely still running 24/7 somewhere.

cues.zh: 呃，如果它们还没被替换掉的话。
cues.en: Uh, if they haven't been replaced.

cues.zh: 所以，呃，第一个概念“长时间”指的是持续运行，而不是只跑一阵子。
cues.en: So, uh, this first notion of extended periods of time means continuously as opposed to just for a burst.

cues.zh: 它们几乎总是在处理信息。
cues.en: They almost always deal with information.

cues.zh: 对，我刚才讲的是哪几类东西？调度。
cues.en: Right, what were the kinds of things I talked about? Scheduling.

cues.zh: 做排期时，你会看过去做过什么，看你的研究数据。
cues.en: And scheduling you look at what you've done in the past, you look at your research data.

cues.zh: 受众会告诉你他们喜欢什么、对什么感兴趣，或者对什么已经厌倦了？
cues.en: What does your audience tell you they, they like or they're interested in or what they're burnt out on?

cues.zh: 你把这些知识结合起来，制定一份日程安排。
cues.en: And you combine that knowledge, um, to make a schedule.

cues.zh: 收益管理会查看过去的销售，以及与特定时段相关的销售和事实。
cues.en: Yield management, looks at the past sales and sales related to particular periods of time and facts about that.

cues.zh: 并生成定价信息。
cues.en: And, uh, produces pricing information.

cues.zh: 选举系统会查看以往的投票记录。
cues.en: Uh, the election system looks at prior vote records.

cues.zh: 人们以前是怎么投票的？
cues.en: How did people vote before?

cues.zh: 这是他们之后会如何投票的重要指标。
cues.en: That is a big indicator of how they're going to vote again.

cues.zh: 当然，背后的算法要复杂得多，但简单来说，你可以说所有这些系统都消费信息，信息对它们至关重要，其中一些还会产出信息。
cues.en: Uh, of course, the algorithms behind that are are much more sophisticated but in, in in a simplified way, you can say all of these systems consumed information uh and it was vital to them and some of them produced information.

cues.zh: 它们会记录自己做过的事。
cues.en: They track the record of what they did.

cues.zh: 也就是下一点：这些系统大多有某种时间跨度很长的记忆。
cues.en: And that's this next point which is that most of these systems have some sort of time extensive memory.

cues.zh: 那个数据库并不是系统的固定输入。
cues.en: That database isn't like an input to the system that's, you know, fixed.

cues.zh: 它会随着系统运行不断被追加内容。
cues.en: It's something that gets added to as the system runs.

cues.zh: 所以这些系统会记住自己做过什么。
cues.en: Uh, so, uh, these systems are, are, uh, remembering what they did.

cues.zh: 而且往往既供自己使用，也供其他程序使用。
cues.en: And they're doing it both for their own consumption and for consumption by other programs quite often.

cues.zh: 它们还要处理现实世界的不规则性。
cues.en: And they deal with real world irregularity.

cues.zh: 我觉得还有一点非常关键，在这个“情境化编程”的世界里。
cues.en: This is the other thing I think that's super critical, you know, in this situated programming world.

cues.zh: 现实世界从来不像你想象的那么优雅。
cues.en: It's never as elegant as you think the real world.

cues.zh: 我讲过那个调度问题：有人整天在监听，就有线性时间。
cues.en: And I talked about that scheduling problem of, you know, there's linear time with somebody who listens all day.

cues.zh: 有人只是早上和下午开车时听，中间隔8小时，这是一拨人；再过一小时又是另一拨人，再一拨。
cues.en: And there's somebody who listens just while they're driving in the morning and the afternoon and 8 hours apart there's one set of people and then an hour later there's another set of people and another set.

cues.zh: 你知道，你得把所有这些时间都考虑进去。
cues.en: You know, you have to think about all that time.

cues.zh: 你可以想出“多维时间”这种优雅的概念，然后说：“哦，我完全没问题——除了周二。”
cues.en: You can come up with this elegant notion of multi-dimensional time and be like, "Oh, I'm totally good, except on Tuesday."

cues.zh: 对吧？为什么？
cues.en: Right? Why?

cues.zh: 嗯，在美国，某些类型的电台节目里有个叫 two for Tuesday 的安排。
cues.en: Well, in the US, on certain kinds of genres of radio, there's a thing called two for Tuesday.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 所以你做了这个排播系统，系统的主要目的就是绝不连续播放同一首歌，甚至不在离上次播放很近的时候再播。
cues.en: So you built this scheduling system and the main purpose of the system is to never play the same song twice in a row, or even pretty near when you played it last.

cues.zh: 也不要在刚播过某位歌手后很快又播同一位歌手，不然有人会说：你就只会播 Elton John，我讨厌这个电台。
cues.en: And not even play the same artist near when you played the artist or else somebody's going to say, all you do is play Elton John, I hate this station.

cues.zh: 嗯，但到了周二，这就是个噱头。
cues.en: Um, but on Tuesday, it's a gimmick.

cues.zh: “周二双播”的意思是，每个播歌的时段，我们都要播两首同一位歌手的歌。
cues.en: Two for Tuesday means, every spot where we play a song, we're going to play two songs by that artist.

cues.zh: 违反你放进系统里的每一条宝贵而优雅的规则。
cues.en: Violating every precious, elegant rule you put in the system.

cues.zh: 而我从未遇到过没有这类不规则之处、或者这些不规则之处不重要的真实系统。
cues.en: And I've never had a real world system that didn't have these kinds of irregularities and where they weren't important.

cues.zh: 呃，情境程序的其它方面，很少像它们自己的小宇宙，能决定事情该怎样。
cues.en: Uh, other aspects of situated programs, they rarely are sort of their own little universe where they get to decide how things are.

cues.zh: 而且它们不需要和其他任何人交互，也不需要和任何人达成一致。
cues.en: And they don't need to interact with anyone else or agree with anyone else.

cues.zh: 几乎所有这类系统都与其他系统交互。
cues.en: Almost all these systems interacted with other systems.

cues.zh: 几乎所有这类系统都会和人交互，有人会坐在那儿说：“现在开始放这首歌”，或者说：“跳过这首歌”，而我们就会想：“好吧，我安排好了那首歌，还围绕你要播放它把一切都协调好了，现在，你知道，DJ 刚说别那么做。”
cues.en: Almost all of these systems interacted with people, somebody would sit there and say, "Start playing this song right now," or, "Skip this song," and we're like, "Well, I scheduled that song and I balanced everything around you playing it and now, you know, DJ just said don't do that."

cues.zh: 呃，选举预测系统有大量屏幕，供用户查看信息、交叉制表、做决策，并为电视上看到的所有内容提供数据。
cues.en: Um, the election projection system has tons of screens for users to look at things and cross tabulate things and make decisions and feeding all the things you see on TV.

cues.zh: 这样人们就能向其他人解释事情。
cues.en: So people can explain things to other people.

cues.zh: 所以，人和与人交流是这些程序的重要部分。
cues.en: So people and talking to people is an important part of these programs.

cues.zh: 它们会长期保持使用。
cues.en: They remain in use for long periods of time.

cues.zh: 这些不是用完就扔的程序。就像我说的，呃，我不觉得我写过的软件里有很多已经没人运行了。
cues.en: These are not throwaway programs, like I said, um, a lot of, I don't know that much of the software I ever wrote has stopped being run by somebody.

cues.zh: 呃，人们还在用它。
cues.en: Uh, people are still using it.

cues.zh: 呃，而且它们还处在一个不断变化的世界里。所以还是那句话，你第一天写它时计划得再好，规则随后也会变。
cues.en: Um, and they're also situated in a world that changes. So again, your best laid plans are there the day you first write it, but then the rules change.

cues.zh: 也许星期四有三个。
cues.en: Maybe there's three for Thursdays.

cues.zh: 我不知道，但当这种情况发生时，你就得改所有东西来应对。
cues.en: I don't know, but when that happens, you go change everything to to deal with it.

cues.zh: 嗯，置身于情境中的另一个方面——我最近想得更多了——就是置身于软件环境和社区之中。
cues.en: Uh, another aspect of being situated and it's one I think I've been thinking about a lot more recently, is being situated in the, in the software environment and community.

cues.zh: 嗯，你知道，你的程序很少是从零写起，所有代码都只为你这个程序而写。
cues.en: Uh, you know, your program is rarely written from scratch with all code that you wrote just for the purpose of the program.

cues.zh: 不可避免地，你会引入一些库。
cues.en: Invariably you're going to pull in some libraries.

cues.zh: 一旦这么做，你就把自己置身于那个库的生态系统中了。
cues.en: And when you do, you've situated yourself in that library ecosystem.

cues.zh: 嗯，这又是另一点。
cues.en: Uh, and that's another thing.

cues.zh: 所以，当我谈论有情境的程序，再看看我讲过自己职业生涯中写过的那些程序，其中一个特别突出，对吧？
cues.en: So, when I talk about situated programs and you look at the programs I talked about having written in my career, one of them really sticks out, right?

cues.zh: 是哪个？
cues.en: What's that?

cues.zh: Closure 编译器。
cues.en: Closure, compilers.

cues.zh: 它们不是这样的。它们完全没有这些问题。
cues.en: They're not like this. They don't have a fraction of these problems.

cues.zh: 它们从磁盘读取一些输入，就能定义整个世界，对吧？
cues.en: They take some input right off the disk, they get to define the whole world, right?

cues.zh: 当你写一门语言时，你会做什么？
cues.en: When you write a language, what do you do?

cues.zh: 写语言时你做的第一件事，就是去掉所有“周二特价”式的东西。
cues.en: The first thing what you do when you write a language, you get rid of any two for Tuesdays.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 你只要，你直接禁止它就行。
cues.en: You just, you can just disallow it.

cues.zh: 对，你会尽量做出最规则的东西。
cues.en: Right, you try to make the most regular thing.

cues.zh: 然后你的编程就只是：好吧，现在我得执行我自己编出来的规则。
cues.en: And then your programming is just, well, now I have to enforce the rules that I made up for myself.

cues.zh: 就像，哇，还有什么比这更容易？
cues.en: It's like, wow, what could be easier than that?

cues.zh: 呃，而且它确实简单得多。
cues.en: Uh, and it really is a lot simpler.

cues.zh: 它们通常不用数据库，不过我觉得它们可能应该用。
cues.en: Um, they don't generally use a database, although I think they probably should.

cues.zh: 它们很少通过网络通信之类之类的。
cues.en: They rarely talk over wires and blah blah blah blah blah.

cues.zh: 所以，编译器、定理证明器之类的东西，不像这些程序。
cues.en: So, compilers and theorem provers and things like that are not like these programs.

cues.zh: 这次演讲的标题是“有效程序”。那 effective 是什么意思？
cues.en: So the title of this talk is effective programs. And what does effective mean?

cues.zh: 呃，意思是产生预期的结果。
cues.en: Uh, it means producing the intended result.

cues.zh: 我真的很想让这个词变得重要，因为我实在受够了“正确性”这个词。
cues.en: And I really want this word to become important because I'm really tired of the word correctness.

cues.zh: 而这里的正确性，说白了，就是让类型检查器满意。
cues.en: where correctness means, I don't know, made the type checker happy.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 也就是说，我在职业工作中写的这些程序，没有任何用户会在乎这一点。
cues.en: That is, nobody, none of my consumers of these programs that I did professionally, care about that.

cues.zh: 对，他们在乎的是程序能按他们定义的“能用”来运行。
cues.en: Right, they care that the program works for their definition of works.

cues.zh: 嗯，但另一方面，我不希望这被理解成：这就是一套随便糊弄的秘诀。
cues.en: Um, on the other hand, I don't want this to be taken as, this is a recipe for hacking.

cues.zh: 对吧？就像随便怎么做，只要能勉强跑就行。
cues.en: Right? Just like do anything that kind of works.

cues.zh: 所以我们必须谈谈“能用”到底是什么意思。
cues.en: So we have to talk about what works means.

cues.zh: 真正有效地完成一项工作，到底意味着什么？
cues.en: What does it mean to actually accomplish a job of being being effective?

cues.zh: 也正是在这里，我想重新夺回“编程”这个名字，或者至少确保我们有一个宽泛的定义，能把 Clojure 这样的语言以及它采用的方法包含进来，因为我认为这些问题很重要。
cues.en: And, and that's where I want to sort of reclaim the name programming, or at least make sure we have a broad definition that incorporates languages like Closure and the approaches that it takes, because I think these problems matter.

cues.zh: 那么，编程到底是为了什么？
cues.en: So what is programming about?

cues.zh: 对我来说，编程就是让计算机在现实世界中发挥作用。
cues.en: I'm going to say for me, programming is about making computers effective in the world.

cues.zh: 这里的“发挥作用”，和我们刚才说的人在世界中发挥作用是一个意思。
cues.en: And I mean effective in the same way we were talking about people being effective in the world.

cues.zh: 要么程序本身发挥作用，要么它们在帮助人发挥作用。
cues.en: Either the programs themselves are effective or they're helping people be effective.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 那么，我们是如何发挥作用的？
cues.en: Now, how are we effective?

cues.zh: 有时我们有效，是因为我们算得很好，比如计算导弹弹道之类的时候。
cues.en: Well, sometimes we're effective because we calculate really well, like maybe when we're trying to compute trajectories for missiles or something like that.

cues.zh: 但大多数时候并不是。
cues.en: But mostly not.

cues.zh: 在人类的大多数领域，也就是人类的各项事业中，我们之所以能发挥作用，是因为我们从经验中学习。
cues.en: Most of the areas of human dome, you know, human endeavor, uh, we're effective because we have learned from our experience.

cues.zh: 并且我们能把这些经验转化为预测能力。
cues.en: And we can turn that, uh, experience into predictive power.

cues.zh: 无论是知道不要踩进大坑、不要掉下悬崖，不要走向咆哮的狮子，还是知道如何向人营销、做这台手术的正确方式是什么，或者这个问题的正确诊断是什么。
cues.en: Whether that's knowing not to step in a giant hole or off a cliff, or walk towards the roaring lion or, uh, how to market to people or what's the right approach to doing this surgery or what's the right diagnosis for this problem.

cues.zh: 嗯，人之所以高效，是因为他们会学习，从经验中学习，并利用这些经验。
cues.en: Uh, people are effective because they learn and they learn from experience and they leverage that.

cues.zh: 所以我想说，高效主要不在于计算，而在于从信息中生成预测能力。
cues.en: And so I'm going to say being effective is mostly not about computation, but it's about, uh, generating predictive power from information.

cues.zh: 你们听我讲过信息，对吧？
cues.en: And you've heard me talk about information, right?

cues.zh: 它关乎事实，关乎实际发生的事情。
cues.en: It's about facts, it's about things that happen.

cues.zh: 对吧？经验，尤其是当我们开始把它带入编程世界时。
cues.en: Right? Experience, especially when we start pulling this into the programming world.

cues.zh: 经验等于信息，等于关于实际发生之事的事实。
cues.en: Experience equals information, equals facts about things that actually happen.

cues.zh: 对吧？这就是世界上成功的原材料。
cues.en: Right? That's what, that's the raw material of success in the world.

cues.zh: 对人来说是这样。对支持人或替代人的程序来说也应该是这样。
cues.en: It is for people. It should be for programs that either support people or replace people.

cues.zh: 这样它们就能做更有意思的事。
cues.en: So they can do more interesting things.

cues.zh: 所以我也想说，对我来说，编程不关乎什么？
cues.en: So I'll also say that for me, what is programming not about?

cues.zh: 它不是关于它自身的。
cues.en: It's not about itself.

cues.zh: 编程不是去证明“类型与你最初的命题一致”这类理论。
cues.en: Programming is not about proving theories about types being consistent with your initial propositions.

cues.zh: 并不是。
cues.en: It's not.

cues.zh: 那本身是个有意思的追求。
cues.en: That's an interesting endeavor of its own.

cues.zh: 但它不是。
cues.en: But it's not.

cues.zh: 这
cues.en: It's

cues.zh: 不是
cues.en: not

cues.zh: 我一直在讲的东西。
cues.en: what I've been talking about.

cues.zh: 这不是我职业生涯中做的事。
cues.en: It's not the things I've done in my career.

cues.zh: 这不是编程对我的意义，也不是我热爱编程的原因。
cues.en: It's not what programming is for me and it's not why I love programming.

cues.zh: 我喜欢在现实世界里做成事情。
cues.en: I like to accomplish things in the world.

cues.zh: Berton Russell 对此有一句很妙的挖苦话。
cues.en: And Berton Russell has a nice snarky comment about that.

cues.zh: 其实他并不是在挖苦。
cues.en: He's actually not being snarky.

cues.zh: 他想抬高数学，说：
cues.en: He wants to elevate mathematics and say,

cues.zh: 数学只关乎自身，这非常重要。
cues.en: it's quite important that mathematics be only about itself.

cues.zh: 一旦你开始越界，对吧，
cues.en: If you start crossing the line, right,

cues.zh: 站在台上说，数学上的，你知道，
cues.en: and standing on stage and saying mathematical you know,

cues.zh: 安全性，类型安全等于，你知道，
cues.en: safety, type safety equals, you know,

cues.zh: 心脏设备安全，
cues.en: heart machine safety,

cues.zh: 按 Berton Russell 的说法，你就是在错误地做数学。
cues.en: you're doing mathematics wrong according to Berton Russell.

cues.zh: 而且这不仅仅是算法和计算，
cues.en: And it's not just algorithms and computation,

cues.zh: 它们很重要，
cues.en: they're important,

cues.zh: 但它们只是我们所做事情的一部分。
cues.en: but they're a subset of what we do.

cues.zh: 所以别误会我。
cues.en: So, don't get me wrong.

cues.zh: 我喜欢逻辑，
cues.en: I like logic,

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: right?

cues.zh: 我写过那些调度系统，也写过那些收益管理算法。
cues.en: I've written those scheduling systems, I've written those yield management algorithms.

cues.zh: 我写过一个数据日志引擎。
cues.en: I've written a data log engine.

cues.zh: 我喜欢逻辑。
cues.en: I like logic.

cues.zh: 我喜欢写系统中那一部分。
cues.en: I like writing that part of the system.

cues.zh: 我通常能负责系统中那一部分。
cues.en: I usually get to work on that part of the system.

cues.zh: 那真的很酷。
cues.en: That's really cool.

cues.zh: 呃，但即便是，你知道，定理证明器或编译器，
cues.en: Uh but even, you know, a theorem prover or a compiler,

cues.zh: 你知道，最终也需要从磁盘读点东西，或者
cues.en: you know, eventually needs to read something from the disk or.

cues.zh: 吐出点东西、打印点东西。
cues.en: spit something back out, print something.

cues.zh: 所以总得有一层逻辑之外的东西来衔接。
cues.en: So there's some shim of something other than the logic.

cues.zh: 但在这种情境化程序的世界里，以及我做过的那些编程中，
cues.en: But in this world of situated programs and the kinds of programming that I have done,

cues.zh: 而且我认为闭包程序员也是这么做的，
cues.en: and I think that closure programmers do,

cues.zh: 呃，那只是程序的一小部分。
cues.en: uh that's a small part of the program.

cues.zh: 程序主要由信息处理主导。
cues.en: Programs are dominated by information processing.

cues.zh: 除非它们有 UI，这种情况下，这周围会有一个巨大的圈。
cues.en: Unless they have UIs, in which case there's this giant circle around this.

cues.zh: 而在这里，它看起来就像一个小点。
cues.en: where this looks like a dot.
